description: Hi I'm Lenny Johnson, a product designer and space lover, and I'm leading the Xenospace team for this contest. We create space tech solutions to solve challenges in Africa. We believe the African continent shouldn't be left behind in the space race. You can learn about what we do here: https://xenospace-beta.vercel.app/
summary:
My Little Red Planet is a kid-friendly Mars exploration and survival game inspired by life-simulation games like Stardew Valley. Set in 2036 at an outpost in the Hebrus Valles region of Mars, players take responsibility for maintaining the habitat, growing food, managing resources, caring for sick crew members, and preparing for environmental emergencies.

The game addresses the Junior Astronaut Trainer challenge by turning real-world Martian living problems into interactive STEM experiences. Players must make meaningful decisions with limited water, oxygen, energy, food and building materials. Every choice has consequences: saving one crop may mean sacrificing another, repairing solar panels may involve radiation risks, and protecting the crew may require sacrificing resources needed for expansion.

This game is important because it makes complex concepts such as sustainability, resource management, teamwork, engineering and life-support systems accessible and engaging for young learners. Rather than simply teaching them about the challenges of living on Mars, it lets them experience the decisions astronauts have to make everyday.
details:
My Little Red Planet by XENOSPACE

Website: https://myredplanet.vercel.app/

Github: https://github.com/bytemojo/my-red-planet.git

All NASA data used i: https://github.com/bytemojo/my-red-planet/blob/visual-pass-a/docs/NASA_SOURCES.md

What does the project do and how does it work?

My Little Red Planet is an interactive, kid-friendly survival and life-simulation game set in 2036 at a NASA research habitat in the Hebrus Valles region of Mars. Players take on the role of the only healthy astronaut after the rest of the crew becomes sick. Their mission is to keep the habitat operational, care for the crew and prepare the base for an approaching solar radiation storm.

Players explore the habitat, repair equipment, maintain life-support systems, grow food in a greenhouse, manage water and energy supplies, communicate with crew members and eventually expand the settlement. They must also wear spacesuits when exploring outside and respond to environmental hazards.

A central feature is the resource-management system. Players regularly face difficult decisions with limited supplies.

What benefits does it have?

The game introduces young players to important STEM concepts through hands-on gameplay rather than traditional lessons. It encourages:

  • Critical thinking and decision-making.
  • Understanding of renewable energy and energy conservation.
  • Knowledge of plant growth, food production and water recycling.
  • Awareness of radiation, solar storms and environmental hazards.
  • Problem-solving, engineering and teamwork.
  • Understanding of the challenges involved in sustaining human life beyond Earth.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make space science accessible, exciting and memorable for children. We want players to understand that establishing a human settlement on Mars involves much more than reaching another planet. It requires careful planning, engineering, scientific knowledge and responsible management of limited resources.

By allowing players to experience the consequences of their decisions, we hope to inspire curiosity about NASA missions, space exploration and future careers in science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

What tools and technologies did we use?

The project is being developed as a digital game using open web frameworks and programmed by AI agents. Alongside game assets, animations, interface design and local save systems. NASA scientific resources and educational materials, including Mars imagery, terrain data, and solar activity information, inform the game's setting and simulated environmental events.

How is the project creative?

We combine the familiar, engaging gameplay of farming and life-simulation games with the challenges of astronaut survival. Instead of simply answering science questions, players actively manage a living Mars habitat. Crops grow over time, equipment can malfunction, crew members have individual needs, and environmental emergencies force players to make difficult choices.

The game also incorporates a wiki that connects gameplay to NASA research.

What factors did your team consider?

We thought about how we could make the game fun as well as teach beginners about real space science and the work NASA is doing. Our team is comprised of Geologists, educators, designers, and programmers.
